claim: MCM8 and MCM9 form a functional helicase complex (MCM8/9) that plays an essential role in DNA homologous recombination repair for DNA double-strand break.
source: MCM8 and MCM9 form a functional helicase complex (MCM8/9) that plays an essential role in DNA homologous recombination repair for DNA double-strand break.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known function of MCM8/9, supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: MCM8/9 is arranged into a heterohexamer through a threefold symmetry axis, creating a central channel that accommodates DNA.
source: The structures reveal that MCM8/9 is arranged into a heterohexamer through a threefold symmetry axis, creating a central channel that accommodates DNA.
evidence: This structural finding is directly observed in the cryo-EM structures presented in the manuscript.

claim: Multiple characteristic hairpins from the N-terminal oligosaccharide/oligonucleotide (OB) domains of MCM8/9 protrude into the central channel and serve to unwind the duplex DNA.
source: Multiple characteristic hairpins from the N-terminal oligosaccharide/oligonucleotide (OB) domains of MCM8/9 protrude into the central channel and serve to unwind the duplex DNA.
evidence: This is based on structural observations from cryo-EM data and functional inference from the positioning of these hairpins.

claim: When activated by HROB, the structure of MCM8/9's N-tier ring converts its symmetry from C3 to C1 with a conformational change that expands the MCM8/9's trimer interface.
source: When activated by HROB, the structure of MCM8/9's N-tier ring converts its symmetry from C3 to C1 with a conformational change that expands the MCM8/9's trimer interface.
evidence: This conformational change is observed in the cryo-EM structures comparing MCM8/9 with and without HROB.

claim: The flexible C-tier ring exhibited rotary motions relative to the N-tier ring, which is required for the unwinding ability of MCM8/9.
source: Moreover, our structural dynamic analyses revealed that the flexible C-tier ring exhibited rotary motions relative to the N-tier ring, which is required for the unwinding ability of MCM8/9.
evidence: This is based on multi-body refinement analysis of cryo-EM data and functional inference about its role in unwinding.

claim: Dysfunction of multiple DNA helicases has been correlated with various human diseases including cancers, Bloom Syndrome, Werner Syndrome, Fanconi Anemia, reproductive deficiencies, and infertility.
source: Dysfunction of multiple DNA helicases has been correlated with various human diseases including cancers, Bloom Syndrome, Werner Syndrome, Fanconi Anemia, reproductive deficiencies, and infertility, etc (Brosh and Matson, 2020; Heyer et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The MCM family contains two subgroups of AAA+ ATPase/helicase complexes, consisting of eight MCM members (MCM2-9).
source: In the human genome, the MCM family contains two subgroups of AAA+ ATPase/helicase complexes, consisting of eight MCM members (MCM2-9) (Maiorano et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the MCM family, supported by citation.

claim: The hexameric MCM2-7 complex plays a vital role in the initiation and elongation of eukaryotic chromosome replication.
source: The hexameric MCM2-7 complex, also known as a replicative helicase, play a vital role in the initiation and elongation of eukaryotic chromosome replication.
evidence: This is established knowledge about MCM2-7 function.

claim: The MCM2-7 complex exhibits high structural flexibility during DNA replication.
source: Previous structural and biochemical studies have revealed that the MCM2-7 complex exhibits high structural flexibility during DNA replication (Yuan and Li, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: MCM2-7 can adopt multiple conformations by interacting with its loaders and activators to form different intermediates, including the helicase-loading intermediate Orc-Cdc6-Cdt1-MCM2-7 (OCCM), the inactive MCM2-7 Double Hexamer (DH) and the active replicative helicase complex Cdc45-MCM2-7-GINS (CMG).
source: It can adopt multiple conformations by interacting with its loaders and activators to form different intermediates, including the helicase-loading intermediate Orc-Cdc6-Cdt1-MCM2-7 (OCCM), the inactive MCM2-7 Double Hexamer (DH) and the active replicative helicase complex Cdc45-MCM2-7-GINS (CMG) (Yuan et al., 2017; Miller et al., 2019; Li et al., 2015; Abid Ali et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous structural studies.

claim: The origin DNA is encircled into the central channel of the MCM2-7 hexamer via the MCM2-MCM5 entry 'gate'.
source: The origin DNA is encircled into the central channel of the MCM2-7 hexamer via the MCM2-MCM5 entry 'gate' (Samel et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: During double-hexamer assembly, the N-tier ring of MCM2-7 rotates by nearly 30° when aligned with the MCM2-7 hexamer in its loading intermediate OCCM.
source: During double-hexamer assembly, the N-tier ring of MCM2-7 rotates by nearly 30° when aligned with the MCM2-7 hexamer in its loading intermediate OCCM (Noguchi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous structural work.

claim: Layers of characteristic hairpin loops inside the chamber of MCM2-7 hexamer, including the helix-2 insertion loops (H2I), the presensor-1 (PS1) as well as β-turn motifs of oligosaccharide/oligonucleotide (OB) domains, contribute to DNA binding and separation.
source: The aforementioned structural studies have also revealed that layers of characteristic hairpin loops inside the chamber of MCM2-7 hexamer, including the helix-2 insertion loops (H2I), the presensor-1 (PS1) as well as β-turn motifs of oligosaccharide/oligonucleotide (OB) domains, contribute to DNA binding and separation (Slaymaker and Chen, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The allosteric communication loop (ACL) conserved in all MCM helicases is important for helicase activity.
source: Additionally, another allosteric communication loop (ACL) conserved in all MCM helicases was also found to be important for helicase activity.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about MCM helicases.

claim: The ACL mediates inter-subunit interactions between the N-terminal DNA processing domain and the C-terminal AAA+ motor domain.
source: The ACL mediates inter-subunit interactions between the N-terminal DNA processing domain and the C-terminal AAA+ motor domain (Sakakibara et al., 2008; Barry et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: MCM8 and MCM9 function as a DNA helicase complex (MCM8/9) in HR-mediated DNA repair for DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) and DNA interstrand crosslinks (ICLs).
source: In contrast to the replicative helicase MCM2-7, MCM8 and MCM9 function as a DNA helicase complex (MCM8/9) in HR-mediated DNA repair for DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) and DNA interstrand crosslinks (ICLs) (Lutzmann et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Cells lacking MCM8 and MCM9 are highly sensitive to DNA cross-linking reagents.
source: Several studies have suggested that cells lacking MCM8 and MCM9 are highly sensitive to DNA cross-linking reagents (Morii et al., 2019; McKinzey et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: MCM8 and MCM9 knock-out mice are sterile and reveal gametogenesis deficiency as well as chromosomal damage due to impaired HR.
source: The MCM8 and MCM9 knock-out mice were found to be sterile and revealed gametogenesis deficiency as well as chromosomal damage due to impaired HR (Lutzmann et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: During HR repair, MCM8/9 was rapidly recruited to the DNA damage sites and colocalized with the recombinase Rad51.
source: During HR repair, MCM8/9 was rapidly recruited to the DNA damage sites and colocalized with the recombinase Rad51 (Park et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: MCM8/9 interacted with the nuclease complex MRN (MRE11-RAD50-NBS1), which was required for DNA resection at DSBs to facilitate HR repair.
source: It also interacted with the nuclease complex MRN (MRE11-RAD50-NBS1), which was required for DNA resection at DSBs to facilitate HR repair (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: HROB (also known as C17orf53 or MCM8IP) has been identified as an essential factor in loading the MCM8/9 complex to the sites of DNA damage and stimulating its helicase activity to promote replication fork progression during DNA recombination and replication.
source: Recently, HROB (also known as C17orf53 or MCM8IP) has been identified as an essential factor in loading the MCM8/9 complex to the sites of DNA damage and stimulating its helicase activity to promote replication fork progression during DNA recombination and replication.
evidence: This is established knowledge about HROB function.

claim: Loss of HROB led to HR defects because it is necessary for the recruitment and activation of MCM8/9.
source: Loss of HROB led to HR defects because it is necessary for the recruitment and activation of MCM8/9 (Hustedt et al., 2019; Huang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The MCM8/9 binding motif (MBM) is embedded in the PRR region and binds to the NTD domains of MCM8/9.
source: It was reported that the MCM8/9 binding motif (MBM) is embedded in the PRR region and binds to the NTD domains of MCM8/9 (Huang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: MCM8 and MCM9 proteins are structurally similar, with an MCM domain at the N-terminus (NTD) and an AAA+ ATPase domain at the C-terminus (CTD).
source: MCM8 and MCM9 proteins are structurally similar, with an MCM domain at the N-terminus (NTD) and an AAA+ ATPase domain at the C-terminus (CTD).
evidence: This is established knowledge about MCM8/9 domain organization.

claim: The NTD and CTD are connected by flexible linkers (N-C linkers), which allow the movement of the AAA+ domain during unwinding.
source: The NTD and CTD are connected by flexible linkers (N-C linkers), which allow the movement of the AAA+ domain during unwinding (Brewster et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The NTDs of MCM8 and MCM9 share an analogous domain organization and can be divided into three domains: the zinc finger domain (ZF), the helical domain (HD), and the OB domain.
source: The NTDs of MCM8 and MCM9 share an analogous domain organization and can be divided into three domains: the zinc finger domain (ZF), the helical domain (HD), and the OB domain.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of MCM8/9.

claim: MCM8 possesses an additional WHD domain in the CTD while MCM9 contains a putative helix-turn-helix (HTH) domain and an extensional C-tail at the C-terminus.
source: In addition to the AAA+ ATPase domain, MCM8 possesses an additional WHD domain in the CTD while MCM9 contains a putative helix-turn-helix (HTH) domain and an extensional C-tail at the C-terminus (Griffin and Trakselis, 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: A 6.6 Å cryo-EM structure of the human MCM8/9 (hMCM8/9) NTD ring was previously reported.
source: In the previous study, we reported a 6.6 Å cryo-EM structure of the human MCM8/9 (hMCM8/9) NTD ring.
evidence: This refers to the authors' previous work.

claim: Crystal structures of MCM8 and MCM9 NTDs separately exhibited conformational changes when assembled into the MCM8/9 hexamer.
source: We also analyzed the crystal structures of MCM8 and MCM9 NTDs separately, which exhibited conformational changes when assembled into the MCM8/9 hexamer (Li et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The gMCM8/9 shares up to 80% sequence homology with the hMCM8/9.
source: The gMCM8/9 shares up to 80% sequence homology with the hMCM8/9.
evidence: This is based on sequence comparison analysis.

claim: The structures of the NTD and CTD were reconstructed at the resolutions of 3.66 Å and 5.21 Å, respectively.
source: Based on the electron density map, the structures of the NTD and CTD were reconstructed at the resolutions of 3.66 Å and 5.21 Å, respectively, and then aligned into a composite structure (Figure 1B, C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on cryo-EM data processing and reconstruction.

claim: The diameter of the NTD ring is ~132 Å and that of the inner channel is ~28 Å which is large enough to accommodate dsDNA to pass through.
source: The diameter of the NTD ring is ~132 Å and that of the inner channel is ~28 Å which is large enough to accommodate dsDNA to pass through (Figure 1C and S5).
evidence: This is based on measurements from the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The assembly pattern of the gMCM8/9 complex with a threefold (C3) symmetry axis is unique among MCM helicases.
source: The assembly pattern of the gMCM8/9 complex with a threefold (C3) symmetry axis is unique among MCM helicases.
evidence: This is based on comparison with other MCM helicase structures.

claim: The assembly pattern of gMCM8/9 differs from that of the eukaryotic MCM2-7 heterohexamer with non-symmetry and the archaeal MCM homohexamer with sixfold symmetry.
source: This assembly pattern differs from that of the eukaryotic MCM2-7 heterohexamer with non-symmetry and the archaeal MCM homohexamer with sixfold symmetry (Li et al., 2015; Fletcher et al., 2003).
evidence: This is based on comparison with cited structures.

claim: A distinguishing feature of the gMCM8/9 is that the helical domain of gMCM8 contains a long α5 helix that protrudes around the hexameric ring.
source: In addition, a distinguishing feature of the gMCM8/9 is that the helical domain of gMCM8 contains a long α5 helix that protrudes around the hexameric ring (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is observed in the cryo-EM structure.

claim: The gMCM8/9 hexamer is the trimerization of the MCM8/9 heterodimer.
source: As our structural analysis revealed that the gMCM8/9 hexamer is the trimerization of the MCM8/9 heterodimer, this leads to the formation of three dimer interfaces within each MCM8/9 heterodimer and three putative trimer interfaces between each neighboring MCM8/9 heterodimer (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the cryo-EM data.

claim: The dimer interface between NTDs of gMCM8 and gMCM9 is largely composed of the β-strands from the OB domain of gMCM9 and the flanking ZF and OB domain of gMCM8.
source: The dimer interface between NTDs of gMCM8 and gMCM9 is largely composed of the β-strands from the OB domain of gMCM9 and the flanking ZF and OB domain of gMCM8.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the interface.

claim: Both the polar and hydrophobic interactions between respective β-strands are responsible for the binding of the MCM8/9 dimer.
source: Both the polar and hydrophobic interactions between respective β-strands are responsible for the binding of the MCM8/9 dimer.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the dimer interface.

claim: The side chains of R220gMCM9 and Q248gMCM9 form hydrogen bonds with the carbonyl groups in the main chains of I172gMCM8 and T226gMCM8, respectively.
source: For example, the side chains of R220gMCM9 and Q248gMCM9 form hydrogen bonds with the carbonyl groups in the main chains of I172gMCM8 and T226gMCM8, respectively.
evidence: This is based on detailed structural analysis of specific residue interactions.

claim: The main chain of T119gMCM9 forms a hydrogen bond with the neighboring carbonyl group in the side chain of D228gMCM8.
source: In addition, the main chain of T119gMCM9 also forms a hydrogen bond with the neighboring carbonyl group in the side chain of D228gMCM8.
evidence: This is based on detailed structural analysis of specific residue interactions.

claim: The benzene ring of F253gMCM9 inserts into a hydrophobic pocket surrounded by residues L179, P217, F181, L201, and Y199 from gMCM8 and W250 from gMCM9.
source: Furthermore, the benzene ring of F253gMCM9 inserts into a hydrophobic pocket surrounded by residues L179, P217, F181, L201, and Y199 from gMCM8 and W250 from gMCM9, which further stabilize the interaction between gMCM8 and gMCM9 (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is based on detailed structural analysis of specific residue interactions.

claim: The interaction within the trimer interface is weaker compared to the strong interaction between the dimer interface.
source: Compared to the strong interaction between the dimer interface, the interaction within the trimer interface is weaker.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural analysis of the interfaces.

claim: The trimer interface is dominated by electrostatic interaction and hydrogen-bonding interactions.
source: The trimer interface is dominated by electrostatic interaction and hydrogen-bonding interactions.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the trimer interface.

claim: The side chain of R152gMCM8 forms salt bridges with both the side chains of D200gMCM9 and D232gMCM9.
source: The side chain of R152gMCM8 forms salt bridges with both the side chains of D200gMCM9 and D232gMCM9.
evidence: This is based on detailed structural analysis of specific residue interactions.

claim: The side chain of K158gMCM8 forms a hydrogen bond with the side chain of E37gMCM9.
source: In addition, the side chain of K158gMCM8 forms a hydrogen bond with the side chain of E37gMCM9 (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This is based on detailed structural analysis of specific residue interactions.

claim: Opening a 'gate' on the trimer interface for DNA loading will be easier than on the dimer interface.
source: Based on the preceding analysis, we assume that opening a 'gate' on the trimer interface for DNA loading will be easier than on the dimer interface.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural analysis showing weaker interactions at the trimer interface.

claim: The NTDs of gMCM8/9 fit well with those of MCM7, MCM3, and MCM5, but rotated slightly in the following MCM2, MCM6 and MCM4 when compared to MCM2-7 in the OCCM complex.
source: As shown in Figure 3A, the NTDs of gMCM8/9 fit well with those of MCM7, MCM3, and MCM5, but rotated slightly in the following MCM2, MCM6 and MCM4.
evidence: This is based on structural superposition analysis.

claim: The minor variation in alignment is due to the opening 'gate' of the MCM5-MCM2 interface in the OCCM complex.
source: This minor variation is due to the opening 'gate' of the MCM5-MCM2 interface in the OCCM complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural comparison.

claim: When superimposing the hexameric gMCM8/9 complex onto one hexamer of the MCM2-7 DH, the two C-tier rings aligned well while their N-tier rings had a ~30° clockwise rotation.
source: When superimposing the hexameric gMCM8/9 complex onto one hexamer of the MCM2-7 DH, we found that the two C-tier rings aligned well while their N-tier rings had a ~30° clockwise rotation (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is based on structural superposition analysis.

claim: The assembly of the MCM2-7 DH induces the conformational change in its N-tier ring.
source: A more plausible explanation is that the assembly of the MCM2-7 DH induces the conformational change in its N-tier ring (Noguchi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The structure of gMCM8/9 was conformationally similar to the structure of the MCM2-7 complex in its loading intermediate OCCM rather than that in the DH.
source: Overall, our structure of gMCM8/9 was conformationally similar to the structure of the MCM2-7 complex in its loading intermediate OCCM rather than that in the DH.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison analysis.

claim: The recombinant MCM8/9 complex alone exhibited limited helicase activity in vitro.
source: This is also consistent with previous findings that the recombinant MCM8/9 complex alone exhibited limited helicase activity in vitro (Huang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The current structure of gMCM8/9 may represent a loading state of MCM8/9 helicase.
source: Therefore, we presume the current structure of gMCM8/9 may represent a loading state of MCM8/9 helicase.
evidence: This is inferred from structural comparisons and functional data.

claim: The HROB-MBM motif was unable to stimulate the helicase activity of hMCM8/9.
source: Using a helicase assay, we found that the HROB-MBM motif was unable to stimulate the helicase activity of hMCM8/9.
evidence: This is based on experimental helicase assay data.

claim: The HROB-CTD, which includes the OB-fold domain, could significantly activate hMCM8/9.
source: However, its CTD, which includes the OB-fold domain, could significantly activate hMCM8/9 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is based on experimental helicase assay data.

claim: The HROB-CTD directly interacts with hMCM8/9 NTD and forms a complex with it.
source: The HROB-CTD not only directly interacts with hMCM8/9 NTD, but also forms a complex with it, as confirmed by the GST pulldown assay (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on experimental GST pulldown assay data.

claim: The 3.95 Å structure of the hMCM8/9 NTD ring was reconstructed with C1 symmetry.
source: And the 3.95 Å structure of the hMCM8/9 NTD ring was reconstructed with C1 symmetry, in contrast to the structure of gMCM8/9, which has C3 symmetry (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on cryo-EM data processing and reconstruction.

claim: The structure of the hMCM8/9 NTD ring underwent a large conformational change when compared to the previously described hMCM8/9 NTD.
source: We also found that the structure of the hMCM8/9 NTD ring underwent a large conformational change when compared to the previously described hMCM8/9 NTD (Li et al., 2021).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison between two conformations.

claim: One of the trimer interfaces in Conformation II was expanded by ~5 Å.
source: In line with our observation, when superimposed these two conformations of hMCM8/9 NTD, we found that one of the trimer interfaces in Conformation II was expanded by ~5 Å (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is based on structural superposition analysis.

claim: The expansion of the trimer interface pushed neighboring MCM8/9 heterodimers to shift to either side.
source: This expansion further pushed its neighboring MCM8/9 heterodimers to shift to either side.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural analysis.

claim: The left dimer translates downward by ~8 Å and tilts by ~6° while the right one shifts by ~7 Å and tilts by ~8°.
source: The left dimer translates downward by ~8 Å and tilts by ~6° while the right one shifts by ~7 Å and tilts by ~8° (Figure 4I and J).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and measurements.

claim: The ZF of MCM8 shifts by ~3 Å to the left, and the ZF of MCM9 shifts by ~4.5 Å to the right, resulting in an overall expansion of ~6 Å.
source: Interestingly, the ZF of MCM8 shifts by ~3 Å to the left, and the ZF of MCM9 shifts by ~4.5 Å to the right, resulting in an overall expansion of ~6 Å (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and measurements.

claim: HROB activates MCM8/9 by inducing a conformational change of its NTD ring.
source: Based on the above observations and the stimulation effect of HROB on the helicase activity of MCM8/9, we propose that HROB activates MCM8/9 by inducing a conformational change of its NTD ring.
evidence: This is inferred from structural and biochemical data.

claim: The OB-hp of gMCM8/9 forms two layers with the three OB-hp of gMCM8 forming the upper layer and the three gMCM9 OB-hp comprising the lower layer.
source: In particular, the OB-hp of gMCM8/9 forms two layers. The three OB-hp of gMCM8 form the upper layer and the three gMCM9 OB-hp comprise the lower layer (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the OB hairpins.

claim: The tip of the gMCM8 OB-hp contains several positively charged residues (K337, K339, K342).
source: Importantly, the tip of the gMCM8 OB-hp contains several positively charged residues (K337, K339, K342) while the gMCM9 OB-hp contains continuous polar residues (H254, Q255, D256) (Figure 5D), which are conserved in hMCM8/9 (R345, K347, K350 in hMCM8 and Q252, Q253, D254 in hMCM9).
evidence: This is based on structural analysis and sequence conservation.

claim: Certain conserved residues from MCM7 and MCM4 OB hairpin loops are involved in the interaction with forked DNA and may contribute to its separation.
source: As seen in the recently reported cryo-EM structure of the S. cerevisiae CMG on a forked DNA, certain conserved residues, such as K364 and K367 from MCM7 OB hairpin, R449 and R451 from MCM4 OB hairpin loop and polar residues Q308 and N307 from MCM3 OB-fold domain, are involved in the interaction with forked DNA and may contribute to its separation (Yuan and Li, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous structural work.

claim: The OB-hps of gMCM8 are capable to close contact with forked DNA and insert their highly positively charged terminal loops into the major or minor grooves of the DNA strand.
source: We artificially docked a forked DNA into the central channel to generate a gMCM8/9-DNA model and found that the OB-hps of gMCM8 are capable to close contact with it and insert their highly positively charged terminal loops into the major or minor grooves of the DNA strand, implying that they could be involved in substrate DNA processing and/or unwinding (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is based on molecular modeling and structural inference.

claim: The ACLs of M. thermautotrophicus MCM (mtMCM) and Sulfolobus solfataricus MCM (SsoMCM) helicases facilitate interactions between NTDs and AAA+ catalytic domains of hexameric helicases as well as modulate the positioning of the OB-hp and then regulate the helicase activities.
source: Several studies have found that the ACLs of M. thermautotrophicus MCM (mtMCM) and Sulfolobus solfataricus MCM (SsoMCM) helicases facilitate interactions between NTDs and AAA+ catalytic domains of hexameric helicases as well as modulate the positioning of the OB-hp and then regulate the helicase activities (Sakakibara et al., 2008; Barry et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The ACLs show a high degree of conservation when performing the superposition of gMCM8 NTD onto the structure of mtMCM.
source: As shown in Figure 5E and F, the ACLs show a high degree of conservation when performing the superposition of gMCM8 NTD onto the structure of mtMCM (Sakakibara et al., 2008).
evidence: This is based on structural superposition analysis.

claim: Key residues Q235, E236 and P249 in gMCM8 (Q294, E295, P308 in hMCM8) are conserved in mtMCM and important for the mtMCM helicase activity.
source: The sequence alignment of the ACLs also highlights some key residues including Q235, E236 and P249 in gMCM8 (Q294, E295, P308 in hMCM8) that are conserved in mtMCM and important for the mtMCM helicase activity (Figure 5E and F Sakakibara et al., 2008).
evidence: This is based on sequence alignment and citation to previous work.

claim: The ACLs are required for the helicase activity of MCM8/9.
source: Thus, we propose that the ACLs are required for the helicase activity of MCM8/9.
evidence: This is inferred from structural conservation and previous functional data.

claim: Both the wild-type (WT) hMCM8/9 complex and its mutants only exhibited limited DNA unwinding activity in the absence of HROB.
source: In the helicase assay, we observed that both the wild-type (WT) hMCM8/9 complex and its mutants only exhibited limited DNA unwinding activity.
evidence: This is based on experimental helicase assay data.

claim: In the presence of HROB, the WT hMCM8/9 exhibited ~ sixfold stimulation of the helicase activity.
source: In the presence of HROB, the WT hMCM8/9 exhibited ~ sixfold stimulation of the helicase activity, while the mutants deleting the tip residues of the hMCM8 OB-hp or mutating that of hMCM9 OB-hp both showed decreased helicase activities.
evidence: This is based on experimental helicase assay data.

claim: Mutants deleting the tip residues of the hMCM8 OB-hp or mutating that of hMCM9 OB-hp both showed decreased helicase activities.
source: In the presence of HROB, the WT hMCM8/9 exhibited ~ sixfold stimulation of the helicase activity, while the mutants deleting the tip residues of the hMCM8 OB-hp or mutating that of hMCM9 OB-hp both showed decreased helicase activities.
evidence: This is based on experimental helicase assay data.

claim: The hMCM8 ACL mutant (hMCM8_E295R) had no significant change in helicase activity even in the presence of HROB.
source: However, the hMCM8 ACL mutant (hMCM8_E295R) corresponding to that in mtMCM had no significant change even in the presence of HROB, implying that the MCM8's NTD doesn't interact with its CTD directly through ACL hairpins (Figure 5G, H).
evidence: This is based on experimental helicase assay data.

claim: The MCM8's NTD doesn't interact with its CTD directly through ACL hairpins.
source: However, the hMCM8 ACL mutant (hMCM8_E295R) corresponding to that in mtMCM had no significant change even in the presence of HROB, implying that the MCM8's NTD doesn't interact with its CTD directly through ACL hairpins (Figure 5G, H).
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental helicase assay data.

claim: The OB-hps of MCM8/9 play an important role in DNA unwinding.
source: Collectively, the above structural analyses and biochemical experiments suggest that the OB-hps of MCM8/9 play an important role in DNA unwinding.
evidence: This is inferred from structural and biochemical data.

claim: The C-tier of MCM2-7 undergoes conformational change coupling with ATP hydrolysis.
source: Since the C-tier of MCM2-7 undergoes conformational change coupling with ATP hydrolysis (O'Donnell and Li, 2018), we propose that the CTD AAA+ domain of MCM8/9 is also mobile for DNA unwinding, serving as a motor domain.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The CTD AAA+ domain of MCM8/9 is mobile for DNA unwinding, serving as a motor domain.
source: Since the C-tier of MCM2-7 undergoes conformational change coupling with ATP hydrolysis (O'Donnell and Li, 2018), we propose that the CTD AAA+ domain of MCM8/9 is also mobile for DNA unwinding, serving as a motor domain.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison with MCM2-7 and structural dynamics analysis.

claim: The electron density of the gMCM8/9 CTD ring is a little blurry and its structure was reconstructed at 5.21 Å.
source: Notably, the electron density of the gMCM8/9 CTD ring is a little blurry and its structure was reconstructed at 5.21 Å (Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 6).
evidence: This is based on cryo-EM data quality and reconstruction.

claim: The MCM8/9 CTD ring reciprocally rotates right and left relative to the NTD ring.
source: As shown in the Video 1, the CTD AAA+ motor ring reciprocally rotates right and left relative to the NTD ring.
evidence: This is based on multi-body refinement analysis of cryo-EM data.

claim: The N-C linkers of MCM8/9, which are 30–40 residues long, are longer than those in MCM2-7.
source: We analyzed the linkers connecting the NTD and CTD (N-C linkers) of MCM8/9 and found that these N-C linkers, which are 30–40 residues long, are longer than those in MCM2-7.
evidence: This is based on structural and sequence analysis.

claim: The N-C linker of MCM3 is the shortest in MCM2-7, which may restrict the rotary motion of MCM2-7.
source: In MCM2-7, the N-C linker of MCM3 is the shortest, which may restrict the rotary motion of MCM2-7 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis.

claim: Both single and combined deletions of N-C linkers have significantly lower unwinding ability than the WT MCM8/9 complex.
source: In the helicase assay in vitro, we found that both single and combined deletions have significantly lower unwinding ability than the WT MCM8/9 complex.
evidence: This is based on experimental helicase assay data.

claim: The presence or absence of HROB had no effect on the reduced helicase activity of N-C linker deletion mutants.
source: The presence or absence of HROB had no effect on this result, indicating that the N-C linkers are required for the MCM8/9 helicase activity (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is based on experimental helicase assay data.

claim: The N-C linkers are required for the MCM8/9 helicase activity.
source: The presence or absence of HROB had no effect on this result, indicating that the N-C linkers are required for the MCM8/9 helicase activity (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is inferred from experimental helicase assay data.

claim: MCM8 and MCM9 mediate cellular resistance to the DNA cross-linking reagent cisplatin.
source: To do so, we employed a chemoresistance assay because MCM8 and MCM9 had been reported to mediate cellular resistance to the DNA cross-linking reagent cisplatin, which induces DNA interstrand crosslinks that are mostly repaired by HR (Nishimura et al., 2012; Morii et al., 2019; Kanemaki, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: MCM8- or MCM9- deficient DT40 cells exhibit significant sensitivity to cisplatin.
source: As shown in the cell-viability assay, we found a notable reduction in survival of MCM8- or MCM9- deficient DT40 cells following cisplatin treatment compared to the WT DT40, indicating that the KO cells exhibit significant sensitivity to cisplatin.
evidence: This is based on experimental cell viability assay data.

claim: Expression of WT MCM8 or MCM9 cDNAs in their respective KO cells almost completely complemented chemoresistance.
source: Expression of WT MCM8 or MCM9 cDNAs in their respective KO cells almost completely complemented chemoresistance.
evidence: This is based on experimental cell viability assay data.

claim: Expression of N-C linker deletion mutants of MCM8 or MCM9 had minimal complementary effects on chemoresistance.
source: In contrast, the expression of their N-C linker deletion mutants had minimal complementary effects (Figure 6C, D, E and F).
evidence: This is based on experimental cell viability assay data.

claim: The N-C linkers of MCM8/9 are required for its cellular resistance to DNA-damaging reagents.
source: These results suggest that the N-C linkers of MCM8/9 are required for its cellular resistance to DNA-damaging reagents.
evidence: This is inferred from experimental cell viability assay data.

claim: MCM8 and MCM9 form a single heterohexameric ring with a centric channel that allows the DNA to pass through.
source: In this study, we reconstructed two structures of the MCM8/9 helicase complex at near-atomic resolution. We found that MCM8 and MCM9 form a single heterohexameric ring with a centric channel that allows the DNA to pass through.
evidence: This is based on cryo-EM structural data.

claim: The OB hairpin loops within the centric channel may be involved in interacting with and separating substrate DNA.
source: The OB hairpin loops within the centric channel may be involved in interacting with and separating substrate DNA.
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis and functional assays.

claim: The N-C linkers of MCM8/9 play important roles in helicase activity.
source: The N-C linkers of MCM8/9 play important roles in helicase activity.
evidence: This is based on experimental helicase assay and cell viability data.

claim: The regulator HROB induces a conformational change of the MCM8/9 NTD ring, which may underlie the helicase activation.
source: Notably, the regulator HROB induces a conformational change of the MCM8/9 NTD ring, which may underlie the helicase activation.
evidence: This is based on structural and biochemical data.

claim: MCM8/9 and MCM2-7 are both MCM proteins with highly conserved domain organization and sequence similarity.
source: MCM8/9 and MCM2-7 are both MCM proteins with highly conserved domain organization and sequence similarity (Maiorano et al., 2006; Maiorano et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The MCM8/9 hexamer is arranged in an alternate mode with the threefold symmetry axis compared to the heterohexameric structure of MCM2-7.
source: Compared with the heterohexameric structure of MCM2-7, the MCM8/9 hexamer is arranged in an alternate mode with the threefold symmetry axis.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison.

claim: The Escherichia coli helicase DnaB exists in a quaternary state with C3 or C6 symmetry and can change the symmetry states reversibly depending on the pH value of the buffers or the presence of nucleotides.
source: Interestingly, it was reported that the Escherichia coli helicase DnaB also exists in a quaternary state with C3 or C6 symmetry and can change the symmetry states reversibly depending on the pH value of the buffers or the presence of nucleotides (Donate et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The symmetry transition of DnaB plays a role in the loading of regulators on DNA and is directly linked to DNA translocation.
source: It has been proposed that the symmetry transition plays a role in the loading of regulators on DNA and is directly linked to DNA translocation (Yang et al., 2002; Núñez-Ramírez et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: MCM8/9 changes its symmetry from C3 to C1 symmetry in the presence of HROB.
source: Similarly, we doubt that MCM8/9 changes its symmetry from C3 to C1 symmetry in the presence of HROB.
evidence: This is based on structural data showing different symmetries.

claim: Helicases may orchestrate the inner channels by controlling the relative positions of subunits, assisting in DNA loading and unwinding.
source: In other words, helicases may orchestrate the inner channels by controlling the relative positions of subunits, assisting in DNA loading and unwinding.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on structural observations.

claim: The OB hairpin loops of MCM3, MCM4, MCM6, and MCM7 form 'dam-and-diversion tunnel' to block and divert the lagging strand from the leading strand.
source: According to recent research, the OB hairpin loops of MCM3, MCM4, MCM6, and MCM7 form 'dam-and-diversion tunnel' to block and divert the lagging strand from the leading strand (Yuan and Li, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The OB-hps of MCM8 and MCM9 are essential for DNA unwinding.
source: For the MCM8/9 complex, the OB-hps of MCM8 and MCM9 are essential for DNA unwinding.
evidence: This is based on experimental helicase assay data.

claim: Three OB-hps of MCM9 form the upper layer, while three OB-hps of MCM8 form the lower layer, suggesting a synergistic mechanism for MCM8/9 OB hairpins to interact with DNA.
source: They form a two-layered structure with threefold symmetry. In which, three OB-hps of MCM9 form the upper layer, while three OB-hps of MCM8 form the lower layer, suggesting a synergistic mechanism for MCM8/9 OB hairpins to interact with DNA.
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis.

claim: The OB-hp loops of MCM8/9 make very close contact with the DNA strand that passes through the channel, capable of inserting their loops into the major or minor grooves of the DNA in a sequential manner.
source: When modeled a forked DNA into the channel, the OB-hp loops make very close contact with the DNA strand that passes through the channel, capable of inserting their loops into the major or minor grooves of the DNA in a sequential manner.
evidence: This is based on molecular modeling and structural inference.

claim: In Conformation II of hMCM8/9 NTD ring, the OB-hps of hMCM8 and hMCM9 lose their C3 symmetry without significant conformational change.
source: While in the Conformation II of hMCM8/9 NTD ring, the OB-hps of hMCM8 and hMCM9 lose their C3 symmetry without significant conformational change.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis.

claim: The symmetry transition of OB-hps could be caused by HROB while inducing trimer interface expansion.
source: This symmetry transition could be caused by HROB while inducing trimer interface expansion.
evidence: This is inferred from structural comparison.

claim: The highly conserved residue F363 from the OB hairpin loop of MCM7 serves as a strand separation pin to unwind forked DNA via making a π-π interaction with DNA.
source: In addition, the highly conserved residue F363 from the OB hairpin loop of MCM7 serves as a strand separation pin to unwind forked DNA via making a π-π interaction with DNA (Baretić et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The highly conserved phenylalanine on the OB-hps of MCM8 and MCM9 (F353 of hMCM8, F251 of hMCM9) will most likely perform functions similar to those found in MCM2-7.
source: The highly conserved phenylalanine was also found on the OB-hps of MCM8 and MCM9 (F353 of hMCM8, F251 of hMCM9) (Figure 5D). They will most likely perform functions similar to those found in MCM2-7.
evidence: This is inferred from sequence conservation and structural similarity.

claim: When MCM8/9 is complexed with the CTD domain of HROB, it becomes more stable and exhibits significantly higher helicase activity.
source: We found that when MCM8/9 is complexed with the CTD domain of HROB, it becomes more stable and exhibits significantly higher helicase activity.
evidence: This is based on experimental helicase assay data.

claim: The HROB CTD domain is about 20 kDa and is composed of a flexible loop and an OB-fold domain.
source: The HROB CTD domain is about 20 kDa and is composed of a flexible loop and an OB-fold domain.
evidence: This is based on structural and sequence analysis.

claim: The flexible loop of HROB containing ~20 amino acids is sufficient to interact with the MCM8/9 complex, but it alone is unable to stimulate the helicase activity of MCM8/9.
source: The flexible loop containing ~20 amino acids is sufficient to interact with the MCM8/9 complex, but it alone is unable to stimulate the helicase activity of MCM8/9 (Huang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work and experimental data.

claim: The OB-fold domain of HROB is required for MCM8/9 activation.
source: Our helicase assay demonstrated that the OB-fold domain of HROB is required for MCM8/9 activation.
evidence: This is based on experimental helicase assay data.

claim: The OB-fold domain of HROB likely helps to load the DNA into the central channel of MCM8/9.
source: The OB-fold domain is a nucleic acid-binding motif that likely help to load the DNA into the central channel of MCM8/9.
evidence: This is inferred from the known function of OB-fold domains.

claim: The expansion of the MCM8/9 trimer interface may involve a transient conformation state to facilitate the DNA entry into the inner channel of the MCM8/9 hexamer.
source: The expansion of the MCM8/9 trimer interface may involve a transient conformation state to facilitate the DNA entry into the inner channel of the MCM8/9 hexamer.
evidence: This is inferred from structural analysis and comparison with MCM2-7.

claim: HROB not only aids in the loading of DNA into MCM8/9, but also acts as an activator, collaborating with MCM8/9 to promote DNA unwinding.
source: Thus, HROB not only aids in the loading of DNA into MCM8/9, but also acts as an activator, collaborating with MCM8/9 to promote DNA unwinding.
evidence: This is inferred from structural and biochemical data.

claim: A dozen structures of MCM2-7-containing intermediates have been resolved including the OCCM, DH, and CMG with/ without DNA.
source: Benefiting from the rapid development of cryo-electron microscopy technology over the past decade, a dozen structures of MCM2-7-containing intermediates have been resolved including the OCCM, DH, and CMG with/ without DNA (Yuan and Li, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The hand-over-hand rotary mode and the 'dam-and-diversion tunnel' model had been proposed for MCM2-7 helicase in DNA translocation and unwinding.
source: Based on these structures, the hand-over-hand rotary mode and the 'dam-and-diversion tunnel' model had been proposed for MCM2-7 helicase in DNA translocation and unwinding (Yuan and Li, 2020; Eickhoff et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The structural dynamics analysis reveals that the MCM8/9 CTD ring rotates relative to the NTD ring.
source: First of all, the structural dynamics analysis reveals that the MCM8/9 CTD ring rotates relative to the NTD ring.
evidence: This is based on multi-body refinement analysis of cryo-EM data.

claim: The length of the MCM8 and MCM9 N-C linkers are surprisingly much longer than those of the MCM2-7 complex, which may permit the rotations of MCM8/9.
source: Second, the length of the MCM8 and MCM9 N-C linkers are surprisingly much longer than those of the MCM2-7 complex, which may permit the rotations of MCM8/9.
evidence: This is based on structural and sequence analysis.

claim: Single-site structure-guided mutations on the ACL loops have no effect on the helicase activity of MCM8/9, supporting the idea that the N-C linkers, rather than the ACL loop, mediated the interaction between the N-tier ring and the C-tier ring of MCM8/9.
source: The fact that single-site structure-guided mutations on the ACL loops have no effect on the helicase activity of MCM8/9 further supports the idea that the N-C linkers, rather than the ACL loop, mediated the interaction between the N-tier ring and the C-tier ring of MCM8/9.
evidence: This is based on experimental helicase assay data.

claim: HROB can convert inactive MCM8/9 into an active helicase by recruiting and inducing a conformational change in the MCM8/9 NTD ring.
source: Last but not least, HROB can convert inactive MCM8/9 into an active helicase by recruiting and inducing a conformational change in the MCM8/9 NTD ring.
evidence: This is based on structural and biochemical data.

claim: The type of DNA substrate unwound by MCM8/9 is unknown.
source: The most pressing issue is that the type of DNA substrate unwound by MCM8/9 is unknown.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: In vivo sequencing and in vitro DNA binding results are required to screen appropriate substrates for MCM8/9.
source: In vivo sequencing and in vitro DNA binding results are required to screen appropriate substrates.
evidence: This is a statement about future research needs.

claim: HROB only stimulates ~60% of the MCM8/9 helicase in vitro.
source: Furthermore, as the HROB only stimulates ~60% of the MCM8/9 helicase in vitro, we believe that other regulators remain to be discover for the full activation of MCM8/9 helicase.
evidence: This is based on experimental helicase assay data.

claim: Other regulators remain to be discovered for the full activation of MCM8/9 helicase.
source: Furthermore, as the HROB only stimulates ~60% of the MCM8/9 helicase in vitro, we believe that other regulators remain to be discover for the full activation of MCM8/9 helicase.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on incomplete activation by HROB.

claim: High-resolution structures of MCM8/9 with DNA in the presence of ADP or ATP are necessary to fully clarify the unwinding mechanism of MCM8/9.
source: Based on these results, the high-resolution structures of MCM8/9 with DNA in the presence of ADP or ATP are necessary to fully clarify the unwinding mechanism of MCM8/9.
evidence: This is a statement about future research needs.

claim: The MCM8/9 complex structures provided in this study will be a rich source of information for further research into the mechanism of DNA helicase in homologous recombination.
source: Despite these limitations, the MCM8/9 complex structures provided in this study will be a rich source of information for further research into the mechanism of DNA helicase in homologous recombination, as well as for the analysis of multiple disease mutations in MCM8/9 associated with premature ovarian failure as well as cancers.
evidence: This is a statement about the significance of the work.
